business_problem: Siemens Healthineers, a medical technologies company headquartered in Erlangen, Germany, aims to pioneer better access to healthcare for patients worldwide by providing technology solutions for its customers’ challenges.
solution_summary: Siemens Healthineers needed a secure, accessible way to host its multimodality imaging software solution syngo.via on the cloud to meet the needs of its longtime customer HT Médica . Siemens Healthineers chose to work with Overon (Part of GRUP MEDIAPRO), an AWS Partner , to host syngo.via on Amazon Web Services (AWS) for HT Médica. During one of their regular meetings, HT Médica expressed the desire to migrate to the cloud to alleviate pressure on its radiologists and reduce costs. “syngo.via on AWS has fulfilled these goals, keeping costs constrained.” “With all the experience we gained and procedures we created hosting this solution on AWS, we can significantly accelerate adoption of the solution for new customers.” Using the cloud-based version of Siemens Healthineers’ solution, HT Médica reduced its spending on hardware and licensing by 50 percent.

solution_components.name: Amazon EC2
solution_components.role: Provides elastic compute capacity for application, analytics, and infrastructure workloads.

solution_components.name: Amazon EC2 G5 Instances
solution_components.role: Provides specialized compute capacity for imaging, graphics, or machine learning workloads.

solution_components.name: Amazon WorkSpaces
solution_components.role: Provides secure cloud desktops for distributed imaging and diagnostic access.

data_flow: To help meet security requirements, maintain data privacy, and meet other compliance needs common to medical groups, the solution uses additional AWS services, including AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS), a service that provides the opportunity for users to create, manage, and control cryptographic keys to encrypt or digitally sign data across applications and AWS services.
business_outcome: This solution is scalable and can be multitenant, meaning several hospitals can use a central infrastructure while keeping their data separate and secure.
metrics: The validation process took 1 year, and after centralizing its radiology information system, HT Médica saw an up to 50 percent reduction in licensing and hardware costs, achieved optimal imaging latency for its radiologists, and increased patient access to medical tests across Spain.

“With all the experience we gained and procedures we created hosting this solution on AWS, we can significantly accelerate adoption of the solution for new customers.” Using the cloud-based version of Siemens Healthineers’ solution, HT Médica reduced its spending on hardware and licensing by 50 percent.
architecture_clues: The company could now scale Amazon EC2 GPUs to replace hardware costs.

The solution uses Amazon EC2 C5 Instances , which are designed for compute-intensive workloads, and Amazon EC2 G4 Instances , cost-effective GPU instances for machine learning inference and graphics intensive applications.
The high-resolution medical image display and low-latency desktops support radiologists’ ability to make diagnoses as if they were working on local machines.
“Optimizing the network using Amazon WorkSpaces and the knowledge of Overon in adjusting certain parameters to decrease the latency as much as possible was crucial to the project,” says Alvarez.
evidence_quotes: Siemens Healthineers, a medical technologies company headquartered in Erlangen, Germany, aims to pioneer better access to healthcare for patients worldwide by providing technology solutions for its customers’ challenges.
Siemens Healthineers had worked with HT Médica, a chain of 23 imaging centers across Spain, for 15 years and recognized the company as a leader in innovation in radiology technology.
During one of their regular meetings, HT Médica expressed the desire to migrate to the cloud to alleviate pressure on its radiologists and reduce costs.

Both companies recognized the importance of developing a secure solution that could maintain the privacy of patient information and comply with strict European regulations while expanding equity of access to high-quality radiology care across Spain.
To meet its customer’s modernization goals, Siemens Healthineers chose to host the main solution it provided for HT Médica, syngo.via, on AWS.
